A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Danceba study. All ten pages of each, including equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original Danceba results on AIST++ in Table 1, component ablations in Tables 2–3, and qualitative dance and alignment visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains the original AIST++ experiments, ablation results, and qualitative visualizations.

M1.justification: Both retain the same PRE phase extraction and cropping, TGCA gating, parallel Mamba architecture, pose codebooks, cross-entropy objective, and autoregressive inference. No procedural or architectural revision is established.

E1.justification: Both conduct all experiments on AIST++ for music-driven 3D dance generation. The same musical styles and qualitative examples remain; newly cited datasets or methods do not expand evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same ten comparators: Li et al., Dance Revolution, DanceNet, FACT, Bailando, EDGE, DiffDance, Bailando++, E3D2, and Lodge. The component and single-Mamba comparisons also remain.

E3.justification: Both retain the 951/40 training/evaluation split, 60 FPS data, forty 20-second evaluation sequences, and identical metrics. v2 clarifies the replacement used in the existing PMMM ablation without establishing a revision to its experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations, parallel-versus-single Mamba comparison, feature and attention visualizations, and dance/alignment examples test the same questions with the same reported evidence. No new robustness test or supplementary analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both identify Table 1's average results and all ablation results as averages over five independent training runs. Neither adds seed values, variability estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative findings are unchanged. v2's explicit 19.0% Divg advantage over Bailando++ restates the previously reported 7.55 versus 6.34; Figure 4 reformats the same dance examples.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation remains substantively unchanged, with no added assumptions, derivations, or proofs. Equation 6 drops the prime from the phase variable while the surrounding description and Equation 7 retain it, introducing a notation inconsistency without establishing different mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The three component contributions, claimed alignment/diversity advantages, introduction's improvement percentages, and conclusion remain unchanged. Replacing 'significantly better' with 'improved' in the abstract does not change the scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 explains the FIDg shortfall through a specific diversity–quality tradeoff with Bailando++, replacing v1's kinetic-fidelity rationale. It adds a fair-comparison rationale for Pose VQ-VAE, makes its diversity limitation conditional, and newly asserts that AIST++ avoids observable biases.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 newly specifies that 'w/o PMMM' replaces PMMM with TGCA layers. This clarifies implementation of an existing ablation; the PDFs do not establish that it changed. Project access information remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds six references, including Listen, Denoise, Action!, Dancing to Music, DeepDance, and a human-motion-generation survey. These modestly broaden the introduction and Section 2.1; the central positioning against Bailando-related methods and Beat-It remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and terminology edits, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and supplements several explanations. Most prose and the order of the six main sections remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from page 4 to page 3, and Figure 4 moves from page 7 to page 6 with reduced size and vertical compression. Tables 2–3 are resized and Figure 6's caption expands. No figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: Specifying the TGCA replacement resolves an ambiguity about the PMMM ablation control, while the expanded Table 1 discussion and related-work coverage improve interpretation and context. The gains are limited: experimental support is unchanged, and v2 introduces a phase-notation inconsistency in Equation 6 and an unsupported assertion about AIST++ avoiding observable biases.
